prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1107; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured reported a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road and stated the other vehicle drifted into their lane as they signaled. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been cooperative so far.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver named on the policy was the operator at the time of loss. The driver is listed on the declarations page and the coverage was active when the incident occurred.

Entry 3: Police report notes the claimant was present in the vehicle at the scene, and the responding officer's account matches the general description of the collision. Two statements from other sides are on file for reference.

Entry 4: Reviewed the scene photographs, which confirm the approximate point of contact on the driver's side and the position of both vehicles after impact. No independent witnesses have come forward to describe how the lane change occurred.

Entry 5: Vehicle damage is mostly consistent with the impact described by the claimant. The repair estimator noted the scrape pattern and panel deformation align with a glancing contact at moderate speed.

Entry 6: Checked prior loss history for the vehicle and found no earlier damage on record. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start date.

Entry 7: The claimant reports pain in the right shoulder following the collision and says the seatbelt tightened sharply on impact. The reported injury appears to match the kind of force expected from this type of contact.

Entry 8: Medical records show the claimant was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and the prior condition appears to be adding to the current complaints. A records request has been sent to the treating provider for clarification.

Entry 9: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, with follow-up visits continuing beyond the usual recovery window. The adjuster will ask the treating clinician for an updated plan of care.

Entry 10: Spoke with the claimant again today and the account of the lane change and the sequence of events matched what was said in the first conversation. The same details came up in every contact so far.

Entry 11: Based on the documentation reviewed, the claim is moving forward with the injury and property components under evaluation. Next steps include obtaining the complete treatment history and scheduling a review once the outstanding records arrive.
